mainTopic: How the word ״לה׳״ excludes or includes the שעיר המשתלח, and why both its מחוסר זמן and מום disqualifications are needed
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about which animals make a person liable for שחוטי חוץ. ״פתח אהל מועד״ limits liability to animals fit for the Temple. ״לה׳״ then excludes the פרת חטאת and the שעיר המשתלח. The גמרא raises a contradiction: another ברייתא uses ״לה׳״ to include the שעיר המשתלח in the rule against an animal that is מחוסר זמן. רבא answers that ״לה׳״ balances the rest of its verse, so it excludes in one verse and includes in the other. The גמרא then asks why that inclusion is needed, since the lottery only works on goats fit for ה׳. רב יוסף first points to חנן המצרי, but that answer is pushed away, so he points to רבי שמעון, who brings a replacement goat without a lottery. רבינא answers instead with a blemished שעיר המשתלח whose status was moved onto another goat. A ברייתא proves that a מום disqualifies the שעיר המשתלח, and a צריכותא shows that both the מום rule and the מחוסר זמן rule are needed.

steps.title: Only animals fit for the Tent of Meeting bring liability
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the word ״קרבן״ alone would include קדשי בדק הבית. The phrase ״ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו״ limits liability to animals fit to be offered in the Temple.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse only said 'offering,' I would include even animals given to the Temple treasury, since they are also called 'offering' (as in 'we brought the Lord's offering'). So the verse adds 'and he did not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.' Anything fit for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting brings liability outside. Anything not fit for it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is narrowing down which animals make you liable for slaughtering outside the Temple. It uses the phrase ״פתח אהל מועד״ to exclude animals that could never be offered on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״קרבן״ is too broad, because even donations to בדק הבית are called ״קרבן״ in the Torah. The added phrase ״פתח אהל מועד״ sets a test: was this animal fit to be brought to the Temple as an offering? If not, slaughtering it outside carries no liability.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for slaughtering outside the Temple applies only to animals fit to be offered at the Temple.

steps.title: ״לה׳״ excludes the פרת חטאת and the שעיר המשתלח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the פרת חטאת and the שעיר המשתלח would still bring liability, since they have some link to the Tent of Meeting. It answers that ״לה׳״ excludes them, because they are not set aside only for ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might exclude only the animals that are not fit for the Tent of Meeting. But then I would not exclude the פרת חטאת and the שעיר המשתלח, which do come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. So the verse says 'to the Lord': only animals dedicated solely to the Lord. These two are excluded, because they are not dedicated solely to the Lord.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible gap in the last rule and closes it. The word ״לה׳״ excludes the פרת חטאת and the שעיר המשתלח from liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ״פתח אהל מועד״ test alone would not exempt these two animals, because they do have a connection to the Tent of Meeting. The ברייתא therefore adds a second test: the animal must be fully set aside for ה׳ as an altar offering. The פרה is burned outside, and the שעיר המשתלח is sent to עזאזל, so both fail this test.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I would exclude'; it presents a possible line of thought
The red heifer (פרה אדומה)
The scapegoat sent away on יום הכפורים
Set aside only for ה׳, meaning brought as an offering to Him

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the שעיר המשתלח or the פרה are not holy. They are exempt from this particular liability (שחוטי חוץ) because their purpose is not an altar offering to ה׳.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for our משנה's ruling that one who slaughters the שעיר המשתלח outside the Temple is exempt. It is also the point the גמרא is about to challenge.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹצִיא אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין רְאוּיִן לְפֶתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: I would exclude these, which are not fit for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,

phrases.english: which is fit to come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting;
therefore the verse says: 'to the Lord' —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds a gap in Step 1's test and fills it with a second word from the verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״לה׳″ excludes the פרת חטאת and the שעיר המשתלח from liability for slaughtering outside the Temple.

steps.title: Contradiction: another ברייתא uses ״לה׳״ to include the שעיר המשתלח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether ״לה׳″ really comes to exclude. It quotes a ברייתא on ״ירצה לקרבן אשה לה׳״ where ״לה׳״ includes the שעיר המשתלח in the rule against animals that are מחוסר זמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does 'to the Lord' really come to exclude? Here is a contradiction. The verse says 'it shall be accepted as a fire-offering to the Lord.' 'Fire-offering' means altar offerings. From where do we know one may not even consecrate an animal that is too young? The verse says 'offering.' And 'to the Lord' comes to include the שעיר המשתלח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from Step 2 by showing another ברייתא that reads ״לה׳״ the opposite way. There, it is used to include the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second ברייתא, the verse about an animal under eight days old (מחוסר זמן) uses ״לה׳״ to teach that even the שעיר המשתלח must be at least eight days old. So ״לה׳״ treats the שעיר המשתלח as being 'for ה׳,' while our ברייתא said it is not 'for ה׳.' The same word cannot both include and exclude the same animal, so the גמרא needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And contrast them'; it introduces a source that seems to contradict
Fire-offerings burned on the altar
'Lacking time'; an animal under eight days old
He should consecrate it
'To include'; the opposite of לְהוֹצִיא (to exclude)

steps.confusionAlert: The two ברייתות discuss different laws: liability for outside slaughter versus the minimum age of an animal. The contradiction is only about what the single word ״לה׳״ says about the status of the שעיר המשתלח.

phrases.english: And does 'to the Lord' come to exclude?
But raise a contradiction:
'It shall be accepted as an offering by fire to the Lord' —
phrases.notes: Leviticus 22:27, about animals under eight days old.

phrases.english: these are the fire-offerings;
from where do we know that one may not consecrate it while it is lacking time?
The verse says: 'offering.'
'To the Lord' — to include the scapegoat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of ״לה׳״ given in Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation that ״לה׳״ excludes the שעיר המשתלח (Step 2).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא uses the same word ״לה׳״ to include the שעיר המשתלח. This shows the שעיר המשתלח is considered 'for ה׳,' which is the opposite of our ברייתא.

steps.title: רבא: the word's job depends on its verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ״לה׳״ excludes in the verse about שחוטי חוץ but includes in the verse about מחוסר זמן, because the other words in each verse already do the opposite job.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There we learn from the context of the verse, and here we learn from the context of the verse. There, ״to the entrance״ comes to include, so ״to ה׳״ comes to exclude. Here, ״offering by fire״ comes to exclude, so ״to ה׳״ comes to include.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction from Step 3. He says ״לה׳״ does not have one fixed job; its job depends on what the rest of the verse is doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the verse about שחוטי חוץ, ״אל פתח אהל מועד״ is broad and would include things like the פרה אדומה and the שעיר המשתלח, so ״לה׳״ must be there to narrow it. In the verse about מחוסר זמן, ״אשה″ is narrow and would leave out the שעיר המשתלח, which is not burned on the מזבח. So there ״לה׳״ must be there to widen it back.

keyTerms.meaning: from the context of the verse
to include
to exclude
an offering burned by fire

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ״לה׳″ means two different things. It means the same thing in both verses. Only its function changes, because it balances whatever the other words in that verse already do.

phrases.english: Rava said:
There, it is from the context of the verse,
phrases.notes: The verse about slaughtering outside (שחוטי חוץ).

phrases.english: and here, it is from the context of the verse.
There, where ״to the entrance″ comes to include,
״to ה׳״ comes to exclude.
Here, where ״offering by fire″ comes to exclude,
״to ה׳״ comes to include.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָתָם מֵעִנְיָנָא דִקְרָא וְהָכָא מֵעִנְיָנָא דִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Contextual reading: the same word works differently depending on the other words in the verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לה׳״ should always either include or always exclude.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לה׳״ counterbalances the surrounding phrase: it excludes after a broad term and includes after a narrow term.

steps.title: Why was a verse needed if the lottery requires fitness anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the need to include the שעיר המשתלח in the rule of מחוסר זמן, since only goats fit for ה׳ can go into the lottery anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason the שעיר המשתלח may not be consecrated while it is too young is that the Merciful One included it. Had He not included it, I would have said the שעיר המשתלח can be consecrated while it is מחוסר זמן. But the lottery only sets a goat apart if it is fit for ה׳!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the contradiction is settled, the גמרא attacks the inclusion itself. It argues that the verse should not be needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the lottery, nobody knows which goat will be for ה׳ and which will be the שעיר המשתלח. So both goats must already be fit for ה׳, which means neither may be מחוסר זמן. The rule would be true even without a verse, so the inclusion of ״לה׳״ seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason is that the Torah included it
an animal too young to be offered, under eight days old
the lottery that decides which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל
fit to be offered to ה׳

phrases.english: The reason is because the Merciful One included it,
but had He not included it, I would have said:
the scapegoat becomes holy even while lacking time.
But the lottery does not set a goat apart
unless it is fit for ה׳!
phrases.notes: Both goats must be fit for ה׳ before the lottery.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי רַחֲמָנָא, הָא לָא רַבִּי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 4 explains how ״לה׳״ includes, this step asks why the inclusion is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that uses ״לה׳״ to include the שעיר המשתלח in the rule of מחוסר זמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lottery only works on goats fit for ה׳, so the scapegoat can never be מחוסר זמן anyway. That makes the verse unnecessary.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the ברייתא follows חנן המצרי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ברייתא follows חנן המצרי, who holds that a replacement scapegoat is brought and paired without a lottery, so the verse is needed for that goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Whose view is this? It is חנן המצרי. As it was taught: חנן המצרי says, even if the blood is already in the cup, he brings a partner goat and pairs it with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge by naming the תנא behind the ברייתא. He points to a case where a scapegoat is chosen without any lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to חנן המצרי, if the שעיר המשתלח dies after the goat for ה׳ was already slaughtered, a new goat is brought and goes straight to being the scapegoat. That goat never entered a lottery, so the rule of ״fit for ה׳״ never applied to it. That is exactly why the verse ״לה׳״ is needed: to make sure even this goat cannot be מחוסר זמן.

keyTerms.meaning: whose view is this?
a תנא who holds the slaughtered goat's blood is not rejected
blood already collected in the cup
pairs, matches up

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Whose view is this? It is חנן המצרי,
as it was taught: חנן המצרי says:
Even if the blood is already in the cup,
phrases.notes: The goat for ה׳ was already slaughtered when the scapegoat died.

phrases.english: he brings its partner and pairs it with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא מַנִּי, חָנָן הַמִּצְרִי הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא whose view creates a case where the verse is needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every scapegoat goes through a lottery, so the verse is unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to חנן המצרי, a replacement scapegoat is paired without a lottery, so the verse is needed to forbid a מחוסר זמן goat.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common גמרא move: when a verse seems unnecessary, find the opinion where it does real work.

steps.title: Maybe חנן המצרי still requires a lottery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back that חנן המצרי only said the blood is not rejected. He may still require bringing two goats and drawing lots.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that you heard חנן המצרי holds there is no rejection. Did you hear him say there is no lottery? Maybe he brings two goats and draws lots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב יוסף's answer. It says we cannot be sure that חנן המצרי skips the lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנן המצרי's clear point is only that the slaughtered goat's blood is not ״rejected″ (דחוי). He might still say two new goats are brought and a lottery is drawn, with the scapegoat chosen from them. If so, the lottery still demands fitness for ה׳, and the original challenge returns.

keyTerms.meaning: say that you heard him say...
rejection: an offering that becomes permanently disqualified
drawing lots
perhaps

phrases.english: Say that you heard חנן המצרי
holds that there is no rejection;
that he holds there is no lottery
did you hear him say that?
Perhaps he brings goats and draws lots.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְחָנָן הַמִּצְרִי דְּלֵית לֵיהּ דְּחוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's claim that חנן המצרי holds a replacement scapegoat is paired without a lottery.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חנן המצרי only rejected the idea of דחויין. Nothing shows he removed the lottery, so the new scapegoat may still need to be fit for ה׳.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two ideas apart: ״no rejection״ means the slaughtered goat's blood stays valid. ״No lottery″ means the new goat is chosen without lots. Holding the first does not prove the second.

steps.title: רב יוסף's new answer: the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף drops his answer based on חנן המצרי. He now says the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who explicitly holds that a replacement goat is brought without a lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: Whose opinion is this ברייתא? It is רבי שמעון's. As a ברייתא teaches: if one of the two goats dies, he brings another one in its place without a lottery. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous answer was pushed away. So רב יוסף finds a different תנא who clearly holds that a new goat can become the שעיר המשתלח without a lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why the verse must include the שעיר המשתלח in the rule of מחוסר זמן. Any goat that goes through the lottery must already be fit for ה׳, so it could never be מחוסר זמן. But רבי שמעון says a replacement goat is brought with no lottery at all. That replacement goat never passes the 'fit for ה׳' test, so the verse is needed to teach that it too must not be מחוסר זמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather — signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming
Whose opinion is this? — used to assign a source to a specific תנא
Its fellow — here, a replacement goat
Without a lottery

phrases.notes: His earlier answer (חנן המצרי) was rejected in step 7.

phrases.english: As it was taught: if one of them died —
phrases.notes: "Them" means the two goats of יום כיפור.

phrases.english: he brings its fellow without a lottery,
the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא מַנִּי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer from step 6, which step 7 rejected, with a new תנא who clearly holds the needed position.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא (רבי שמעון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every שעיר המשתלח passes through the lottery, so it is automatically fit for ה׳ and the verse is unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון, a replacement goat becomes the שעיר המשתלח without a lottery, so the verse is needed to exclude a goat that is מחוסר זמן.

steps.title: רבינא's answer: a blemished goat whose status was transferred
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers in a way that works for everyone. The case is a שעיר המשתלח that became blemished, and its status was transferred onto another goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: the verse is needed for a case where the goat became blemished, and he redeemed it onto another goat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different answer that does not depend on רבי שמעון. In his case, a new goat becomes the שעיר המשתלח without any lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a goat gets a מום, its holy status can be transferred (חילול) onto a different goat. That new goat takes over the role directly, with no lottery, according to everyone. So the verse is needed to teach that this new goat must not be מחוסר זמן.

keyTerms.meaning: It became blemished (got a מוּם)
He redeemed it, moving its holiness onto something else
Onto another (animal)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer assumes that a מום actually disqualifies the שעיר המשתלח. That assumption is not obvious, because this goat is never offered on the מזבח. The very next step questions it.

phrases.english: Ravina said: for example, where it became blemished
phrases.notes: "It" is the שעיר המשתלח, after it was chosen by lottery.

phrases.english: and he redeemed it onto another.
phrases.notes: The new goat takes on its status without a new lottery.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר, כְּגוֹן שֶׁהוּמַם וְחִילְּלוֹ עַל אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the question of step 5. It works even without רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining a specific case (אוקימתא) where no lottery happens according to everyone
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every שעיר המשתלח goes through a lottery, so the verse is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: If a blemished שעיר המשתלח is redeemed onto another goat, the new goat needs no lottery. The verse is needed for that goat.

steps.title: How do we know a מום disqualifies the שעיר המשתלח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that a מום disqualifies the שעיר המשתלח. רבינא's answer depends on this.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you say that a blemish disqualifies it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check the assumption behind רבינא's answer. This sets up the next step, which brings a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a מום disqualifies an animal because it cannot be offered on the מזבח. The שעיר המשתלח is sent away and never goes on the מזבח, so why should a מום matter? Without a source, רבינא's case would never happen.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you say this? — a request for a source
Disqualifies
A blemish (Aramaic for מוּם)

phrases.english: And from where do you say that a blemish disqualifies it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the hidden assumption in רבינא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a מום disqualifies the שעיר המשתלח, even though it is not offered on the מזבח.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins: blemished fats, even partly, may not be offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the verse about blemished animals. It starts by learning that their fats, even some of them, may not be burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "And you shall not give a fire-offering of them" — these are the fats. I only know this for all of them. From where do I know it for some of them? The verse says "of them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא that will answer the question. This first part goes through the verse word by word and sets up the key word ״לה׳״ that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ב) forbids offering blemished animals. The ברייתא reads "fire-offering" as the fats burned on the מזבח. The extra word ״מהם״ ("of them") teaches that even burning part of the fats is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A fire-offering — what is burned on the מזבח
The fats that are burned on the מזבח
Some of them (part of them)
The verse teaches — introduces the proof from a word in the verse

phrases.english: As it was taught: "And a fire-offering you shall not give of them"
these are the fats.
I only have (the rule for) all of them;
from where (do we know) some of them?
The verse says: "of them."
phrases.notes: "Of them" means even a part of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 10 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a מום disqualifies the שעיר המשתלח (the proof is completed in the next step)

steps.title: ״לה׳״ includes the שעיר המשתלח in the מום rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: ״מזבח״ refers to sprinkling blood, and ״לה׳״ includes the שעיר המשתלח. So a מום disqualifies it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The altar" — this is the sprinkling of the blood. "To ה׳" — this comes to include the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline that answers the question of step 10. The word ״לה׳״ brings the שעיר המשתלח under the rule that a blemished animal is disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first adds that the blood of a blemished animal may not be sprinkled on the מזבח. Then the extra word ״לה׳״ teaches that even the שעיר המשתלח, which never reaches the מזבח, is disqualified by a מום. This supports רבינא's case: a blemished שעיר המשתלח must be replaced.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
To include (to add something to the rule)
The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why the verse must include the שעיר המשתלח in the rule of מחוסר זמן. רב יוסף says the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון: a replacement for a dead goat comes without a lottery. רבינא says it is a blemished goat whose status was redeemed onto another goat. That case works because ״לה׳″ in the blemish verse includes the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.whyThisMatters: Here again ״לה׳″ works to include, not exclude, just as in the מחוסר זמן verse from step 4. This shows that the שעיר המשתלח is treated like a dedicated animal in some ways, even though it is not offered on the מזבח.

phrases.english: "The altar" — this is the sprinkling of blood.
"To the Lord" — to include the scapegoat.
phrases.notes: This is the actual answer: a blemish disqualifies the שעיר המשתלח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא started in step 11 and gives the actual answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לה׳″ in ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ב includes the שעיר המשתלח in the rule that a מום disqualifies an animal.

steps.title: Both disqualifications must be written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the Torah needed to teach both that a בעל מום disqualifies the שעיר המשתלח and that a מחוסר זמן disqualifies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to teach that a blemished goat is disqualified, and it was also necessary to teach that a goat that is too young is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a short claim that both rules about the שעיר המשתלח are needed. This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא will explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now have two disqualifications for the שעיר המשתלח. בעל מום comes from the ברייתא we just saw (steps 11–12). מחוסר זמן comes from the ברייתא quoted in step 3 (״ירצה לקרבן אשה לה׳״). A beginner might think one rule is extra because the other could teach it. The גמרא announces that each one is needed on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
To write (for the Torah to teach it)
An animal with a blemish
An animal 'lacking time': less than eight days old, so too young to be offered

steps.confusionAlert: מחוסר זמן does not mean the animal is late or old. It means it has not yet reached the minimum age (eight days) to be offered.

phrases.english: And it is necessary to write blemished,
phrases.notes: The rule we just learned from the ברייתא

phrases.english: and it is necessary to write lacking time.
phrases.notes: The rule from the ברייתא in step 3, where ״לה׳״ includes the שעיר המשתלח in the rule of מחוסר זמן

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִיכְתַּב בַּעַל מוּם, וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִיכְתַּב מְחוּסַּר זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving that a מום disqualifies the שעיר המשתלח, the גמרא explains why this source is not extra, given the separate source for מחוסר זמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the בעל מום and the מחוסר זמן disqualifications for the שעיר המשתלח are necessary.

steps.title: Why a too-young rule alone would not teach the blemish rule
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had taught only מחוסר זמן, we would have said that the reason is that the animal's time has not yet come. A בעל מום has reached its time, so we would have thought it is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written only 'too young,' I would have said that the reason is that its time has not yet arrived. But a blemished animal, whose time has already arrived, I would say is not disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half: the מחוסר זמן rule alone could not teach us the בעל מום rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason a מחוסר זמן is disqualified is that the animal is not yet ready, so its time has not come. A blemished animal is old enough, so that reason does not apply to it. Without a separate source, we would have allowed a blemished שעיר המשתלח.

keyTerms.meaning: For if
'The Merciful One': a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the Torah
Its time has arrived
I would say not (this rule would not apply)

phrases.english: For if the Merciful One had written only 'lacking time' —
that is because its time has not come,
phrases.notes: It is not yet fit to be consecrated for this purpose

phrases.english: but a blemished one, whose time has come —
I would say it is not disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the claim in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחוסר זמן rule is based on the animal not yet being ready, which does not apply to a בעל מום, so a separate source is needed for מום.

steps.title: Why a blemish rule alone would not teach the too-young rule, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had taught only בעל מום, we would have said that the reason is that a blemished animal is repulsive. A מחוסר זמן is not repulsive, so we would have thought it is fine. Therefore both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written only 'blemished,' I would have said that the reason is that it is repulsive. But a too-young animal, which is not repulsive, I would say is not disqualified. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half and then concludes: each rule teaches something the other cannot, so both are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל מום is disqualified because it is מאיס, meaning unfit and repulsive to offer to ה׳. A young animal is healthy and whole, so that reason does not apply to it. Each rule rests on a different reason, so neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of
Repulsive or disgusting: unfit to bring before ה׳
It is necessary: the closing word of a צריכותא

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכותא shows that two similar teachings are both needed because each has its own reason. A מחוסר זמן is disqualified because it is not yet ready. A בעל מום is disqualified because it is repulsive. Neither reason covers the other case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the support for רבינא's answer. A מום truly disqualifies the שעיר המשתלח, and that teaching is not extra.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'blemished' —
that is because it is repulsive,
but one lacking time, which is not repulsive —
I would say it is not disqualified,
therefore both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror-image reasoning to step 14 and closes the צריכותא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both disqualifications of the שעיר המשתלח are needed, because each rests on a different reason: 'not yet ready' versus 'repulsive'.
